name: Sanat Kumaras
role: Four eternal child-sages, mind-born sons of Brahma
summary: The Kumaras Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana and Sanatkumara are mind-born sons of Brahma who stay as five-year-old boys. They are great teachers of yoga and devotion.
about: According to the Puranas, the Kumaras were the first beings born from Brahma's mind. Asked to help create the world, they chose lives of devotion and wandered the universe teaching. The Chandogya Upanishad shows Sanatkumara teaching Narada about the Self, and the Mahabharata and Bhagavata Purana record his discourses. The Bhagavata Purana tells how they were stopped at Vaikuntha's gate, which led to the three births of Jaya and Vijaya. Shaiva tradition says Shiva taught them as Dakshinamurti, and the Nimbarka tradition traces its lineage to them. Texts name the group differently, with Sanatsujata sometimes in place of Sanatana.
kidSummary: The Sanat Kumaras are four brothers who are said to look like little boys forever, though they are very wise. They walk through the worlds teaching about kindness, devotion and the Self. Their story at Vishnu's gate is one of the best known in the Puranas.

story.title: Four boys, born of thought
story.text: The Puranas say Brahma imagined four sons, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana and Sanatkumara. They appeared as children and stayed five years old.

story.title: A different path
story.text: Brahma asked them to help create the world. The Kumaras instead chose to wander, teach and think about the Divine.

story.title: At Vaikuntha's gate
story.text: The Kumaras visit Vishnu's home and pass six gates. At the seventh, the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya stop them.

story.title: The curse and the choice
story.text: The sages curse the gatekeepers to be born on earth. Vishnu gives them a choice, and they pick three lives as his foes so they can return sooner.

story.title: A teacher for Narada
story.text: In the Chandogya Upanishad, Sanatkumara teaches the learned Narada that knowing many subjects is not the same as knowing the Self.

teaches: Kindness and respect apply to everyone, young or old
Learning is more than memorising names

facts.text: The four Kumaras are usually named Sanaka ('ancient'), Sanandana ('ever-joyful'), Sanatana ('eternal') and Sanatkumara ('ever-young').
Texts most often describe the Kumaras as staying about five years old forever, though some say four. Even so, they studied the Vedas from childhood and are called great jnanis and yogis.
Texts say the Kumaras dwell in Janaloka or in Vishnu's abode Vaikuntha. They keep chanting 'Hari Sharanam', meaning refuge in Vishnu, and praising Vishnu is said to be their only food.
In the Bhagavata story, the Kumaras passed six gates of Vaikuntha freely. At the seventh, the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya laughed and stopped them, and the Kumaras cursed them to be born on earth.
Vishnu could not undo the curse but let Jaya and Vijaya choose seven lives as his devotees or three as his foes. They chose three, to return to him sooner.
The three births are Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu, then Ravana and Kumbhakarna, then Shishupala and Dantavakra. Their power shrank from ruling the earth to a region to a royal family.
In temples, Jaya and Vijaya are carved as four-armed gatekeepers at Vishnu shrines such as Tirumala, Puri and Srirangam. They hold a discus, conch and mace, and a sword in place of Vishnu's lotus.
Chandogya Upanishad chapter 7 has the sage Narada asking Sanatkumara to teach him about the Self. Sanatkumara first asks what he already knows.

Narada lists his learning: the four Vedas, grammar, mathematics, astronomy, politics, warfare, fine arts, snake lore and ghost lore. Sanatkumara says it is all words and names, and Narada admits none of it has taught him about the Self.
Shaiva tradition says the Kumaras learned the highest truth from Shiva as Dakshinamurti, who taught in silence with a hand gesture, the chin mudra, joining thumb and forefinger.
In the Valmiki Ramayana, the minister Sumantra says Sanatkumara had foretold that the sage Rishyasringa would one day help King Dasharatha obtain sons.
The Bhagavata Purana says the Kumaras' refusal to help create the world displeased Brahma, and that his anger gave rise to the deity Shiva.
Some texts, including the Devi Bhagavata and Bhavishya Puranas, say the Kumaras appeared even before the Brahma of the present age.

In the Mahabharata, Vidura sends the worried Dhritarashtra to the eternal sage Sanatsujata, who is sometimes counted as one of the Kumaras. Vidura calls him by meditating on him, and the sage appears and teaches that distraction is a kind of death.
The Bhagavata Purana counts the Kumaras among its twelve mahajanas, great devotees who were liberated from birth yet still became drawn to the worship of Vishnu.
Sanatkumara is said to have taught the young Bhishma the mental and spiritual sciences.
The first part of the Naradiya Purana has four sections, and each is told to Narada by one of the four Kumaras. Narada then passed the teaching to Vyasa, who wrote it down.

The Kumaras go by several group names, such as Chatursana, 'the four with names beginning Sana', and Sanakadi, 'Sanaka and the others'. Some lists add a fifth Kumara named Ribhu, and the Mahabharata names seven mind-born sons.
A text called the Sanatkumara Samhita, with 59 chapters, is attributed to Sanatkumara. It is counted as part of the Shiva Purana and also as a Pancharatra text of Vishnu devotees.
In each of the three lives of Jaya and Vijaya, a different avatar of Vishnu ends them. Varaha and Narasimha do it in the first, Rama in the second and Krishna in the third.
Different Puranas give different parents for Jaya and Vijaya. The Brahmanda Purana calls them sons of Kali, while the Padma Purana calls them sons of Kardama and Devahuti.

quiz.q: Who is the father of the four Kumaras in the Puranas?
quiz.why: They were born from Brahma's mind.

quiz.q: How old do the Kumaras always appear?
quiz.why: Texts describe them as five-year-old boys forever.

quiz.q: Who taught Narada in the Chandogya Upanishad?
quiz.why: Sanatkumara taught Narada about the Self.

quiz.q: Which gatekeepers did the Kumaras curse?
quiz.why: Jaya and Vijaya guarded Vishnu's seventh gate.

quiz.q: How did Shiva teach the Kumaras as Dakshinamurti?
options: In silence with a hand gesture
quiz.why: He used the chin mudra without speaking.
